study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Hua et al., Biological Psychiatry: Cognitive Neuroscience and Neuroimaging, 2025
study_identification_part.si4_title: Adjustment of Regional Cortical Thickness Measures for Global Cortical Thickness Obscures Deficits Across the Schizophrenia Spectrum: A Cautionary Note About Normative Modeling of Brain Imaging Data

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To demonstrate that adjusting regional cortical thickness for global cortical thickness attenuates or eliminates true disease-related effects in schizophrenia-spectrum cohorts, and to caution against incorporating global thickness as a mandatory covariate in normative modeling tools.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Adjusting regional cortical thickness for global thickness obscures or eliminates disease-related regional deficits, whereas ICV adjustment preserves expected deficit patterns.
